name: Doltgres
tagline: Version-controlled SQL database with PostgreSQL compatibility: branch, diff and merge your tables.
description: Doltgres (DoltgreSQL) is DoltHub's PostgreSQL-flavored sibling of Dolt. It reuses Dolt's prolly-tree storage engine and Git-style commit graph, but speaks the PostgreSQL wire protocol and dialect, so psql, Postgres drivers and ORMs can connect while you branch, diff, merge and time-travel over tables with SQL functions. It reached 1.0 in August 2026 and DoltHub now calls it production-ready, though its Postgres coverage (extensions, some types and catalog behavior) is still narrower than real PostgreSQL. It suits teams in the Postgres ecosystem that need data versioning and review workflows more than raw throughput.

pricing.notes: Engine is free; hosted options from DoltHub.

scale.notes: Single primary with replicas via remotes; history grows with commits.

strengths: Git-style branch, diff and merge of tables from SQL
Works with psql and standard Postgres drivers
Shares Dolt's mature versioned storage engine
Clone and push databases between remotes
weaknesses: Only a subset of PostgreSQL extensions, types and catalog features
Slower than PostgreSQL for high-volume OLTP
Young 1.x product with a short production record
useCases: Versioned reference data for Postgres-based apps
Safe data migrations tested on branches
Agent or CI sandboxes that branch data
notIdealFor: Apps relying on Postgres extensions such as PostGIS or pgvector
